check.population: every event, message, topic and consumer that crosses an asynchronous boundary
check.freshness: a verdict stands until an event schema, a consumer or the delivery guarantee changes
check.refusal: the schema registry, idempotency test or workflow test fails the change that breaks delivery or contract
check.observation: published schemas, consumer registrations, and redelivery, lag and dead-letter counts from the broker
check.evidence: none: the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it
check.authority: the published schema and the delivery guarantee, which every producer and consumer conforms to

records.name: Event-Driven Architecture
records.definition: A convention of connecting services through published events, with each consumer reacting independently of the producer.

records.name: Publish/Subscribe Pattern
records.definition: A design pattern in which publishers send messages to a topic and every subscriber to that topic receives them.

distinctFrom.reason: A message queue holds messages until they are acknowledged, while the consumer is the component that takes and processes them.

records.name: Message Queue
records.definition: A mechanism that holds messages durably until a consumer takes and acknowledges each one.
detected_by: synchronous blocking chains for async work

exemplar.before: for (const foo of foos) await processFoo(foo);
exemplar.after:
for (const foo of foos) await fooQueue.enqueue({ type: "ProcessFoo", foo });
fooWorker.consume(fooQueue, message => processFoo(message.foo));

records.name: Message Broker
records.definition: Descriptive data about topics, queues and routing rules, held by an intermediary service that delivers messages between producers and consumers.
detected_by: direct service calls in async workflows

records.name: Event Bus
records.definition: A mechanism that dispatches each emitted event to the handlers registered for its type.

exemplar.before:
fooEditor.onSave = foo => fooView.refresh(foo);
fooEditor.onDelete = id => fooView.remove(id);

records.name: Event Stream
records.definition: A mechanism that keeps events in an ordered, replayable log that consumers read from their own offset.

exemplar.after:
const stream = fooEvents.stream(fooId);
for await (const event of stream) fooProjection.apply(event);

distinctFrom.reason: Event sourcing stores state as its events, while CQRS separates the command model from the query model whatever the storage.
Event sourcing rebuilds state by replay, while an append-only log is the storage it replays from.
Event sourcing makes events the source of state, while domain events can be published with state stored some other way.
Event sourcing is how state is stored, while a saga is how a distributed transaction is coordinated.

records.name: Event Sourcing
records.definition: A design pattern that stores state as the sequence of events that produced it and rebuilds current state by replaying them.

exemplar.before:
type FooRow = { id: FooId; name: string; status: string };
await fooTable.update(foo);

distinctFrom.reason: CQRS splits the write model from the read model, while a saga sequences local transactions with compensations.

records.name: Command Query Responsibility Segregation (CQRS)
records.definition: A design pattern that separates the model that handles commands from the model that answers queries.

records.name: Domain Events
records.definition: A design pattern that records each significant change in the domain as an event named in the domain's language.

records.name: Integration Events
records.definition: A design pattern that publishes a versioned public event, mapped from an internal domain event, for consumers outside the service.

records.name: Asynchronous Communication
records.definition: A design rule that work the caller does not need at once is sent as a message, so the caller does not wait on it.

exemplar.before:
const bar = await barService.createFromFoo(foo);
const baz = await bazService.createFromBar(bar);
exemplar.after:
await outbox.append({ type: "FooCreated", fooId: foo.id });
return { accepted: true, fooId: foo.id };

distinctFrom.reason: Eventual consistency promises only that replicas converge, while causal consistency also promises that no effect is read before its cause.

records.name: Eventual Consistency
records.definition: A conceptual representation of a consistency guarantee in which replicas and projections converge once updates stop arriving.

records.name: Saga Pattern
records.definition: A design pattern that runs a cross-service transaction as a sequence of local steps, each paired with a compensating step.

records.name: Outbox Pattern
records.definition: A design pattern that writes an outgoing message in the same local transaction as the state change, and a relay publishes it afterwards.

exemplar.before:
await fooStore.save(foo);
await eventBus.publish({ type: "FooSaved", fooId: foo.id });

records.name: Compensating Transaction
records.definition: A mechanism that undoes the business effect of a completed step when a later step of the workflow fails.

distinctFrom.reason: An append-only log is the storage shape that never rewrites an entry, while domain events are what gets recorded, named in the domain's language.

records.name: Append-Only Log
records.definition: A design pattern that records history as immutable entries added at the end of the log.

records.name: Dead-Letter Queue
records.definition: A design pattern that moves a message which keeps failing into a separate queue, where it can be inspected and reprocessed.
detected_by: retry storms on a single poison message

records.name: Idempotent Consumer
records.definition: A design pattern in which a consumer records each message it has processed, so a redelivered message has no second effect.

records.name: Competing Consumers
records.definition: A design pattern in which several consumers read from one queue, and each message goes to only one of them.
detected_by: queue depth rising with a single processor
